chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his uncle, who said: Ahmad ibn Hammad ibn Zuhayr al-Qurashi narrated to me from Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'ir from Abu al-Sakheef al-Arajani, who said: Umar ibn Abdillah ibn Talhah al-Nahdi narrated to me from his father, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he mentioned a hadith and narrated it to us. He said: So we went with him, meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), until we reached al-Ghariyy. He said: So he came to a place and prayed. Then he said to Isma'il: 'Rise and pray at the head of your father, al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' I said: 'Is it not that his head was taken to ash-Sham?' He said: 'Yes, but so-and-so, our mawla, stole it and brought it and buried it here.'

key_terms.إِلَى الشَّامِ: To Syria (Damascus), where the head was historically taken
key_terms.الْغَرِيِّ: Al-Ghariyy, a location in Kufa known for the burial of Imam al-Husayn's head
key_terms.رَأْسِ أَبِيكَ: The head of your father, referring to Imam al-Husayn
key_terms.مَوْلاَنَا: Our mawla (client/freedman or follower), referring to a specific companion

ai.seo_question: Where is the head of Imam al-Husayn buried according to this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the spiritual significance of al-Ghariyy in Kufa as a site of intercession and burial, specifically linking it to Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) declaration that a mawla retrieved Imam al-Husayn’s (peace be upon him) head from Syria for interment there. It underscores the Shia belief in the physical presence of the Ahl al-Bayt’s relics in Iraq, reinforcing the sanctity of Kufa and the practice of praying at these specific locations to draw closer to the Imams. The narrative also illustrates the continuity of the Imamate’s connection to the martyrdom of al-Husayn, serving as a theological anchor for Shia devotion and pilgrimage (ziyarat).
